newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares rise with dollar, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: German shares rise with dollar, trade thin.

text.p: German shares posted gains on modest volumes on Tuesday, heartened by an upbeat close on Wall Street overnight, the stable dollar and the Bundesbank's reassuring decision not to raise a key interest rate.
At the end of bourse trade the DAX index of 30 German blue-chips stood at 4,363.09 points, up 29.96 points.
The market posted further gains in thin afternoon electronic trade dealings, with the IBIS DAX ending the post-bourse session at 4,377.51, up one percent.
The overall mood was lifted by the Bundesbank's decision to leave its key money market rate, the repo, unchanged, against isolated expectations that it would tighten its policy today.
But dealers said it was difficult to determine a real trend. "This is summer lull stuff," said a Munich dealer.
"People are a bit wary of some really crucial reports due in the U.S," he added, referring to key inflation data due on Wednesday.
Among the day's best performers was retailer Karstadt AG, which was among the top gainers in bourse and ended up 13.50 marks at 711.50 marks.
The Schickedanz retail group said that it planned to buy stakes in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG, but said its aim was not to take over the firm.
The move was viewed positively by the markets.
Other shares in the news included Henkel KGaA which ended up four marks at 104.50 marks after it released interim results.
Henkel's pretax profit rose 10 percent to 438 million marks from 397 million in the first half of 1997, while group sales rose to 9.784 billion marks from 8.039 billion marks.

Otherwise the main drivers behind the DAX index were the banks. Bankgesellschaft Berlin ended up 3.15 marks at 51.90 marks, Deutsche Bank AG was up 2.30 marks at 119.70 marks and Dresdner Bank AG was up 2.20 marks at 83.70 marks.
Banks have been consistently in vogue in recent weeks among persistent talk of consolidation to come.
